question.problem: Find the remainder when $p(x)=2{x}^{2}-4x+4$ is divided by $5-x.$
question.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $(5-x)=-(x-5),$ the remainder equals $p(5).$ 

Evaluating $p(5)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}p(5) & =2\cdot {5}^{2}-4\cdot 5+4 \\  & =50-20+4 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$

So, when $p(x)$ is divided by $(5-x)$ the remainder is $34.$

**Note:** We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

|  | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $5$ | $2$ | $-4$ | $4$ |
|  | $↓$ | $10$ | $30$ |
|  | $2$ | $6$ | $34$ |
